summary: Layered red rice, avocado, shaved red pepper and baby lettuces in a ring mold, topped with crispy burdock chips made in the microwave, gomashio and a sesame, miso and yuzu dressing.
glance: microwave 30 seconds at a time until shriveled and crispy
white miso, lime or yuzu juice, toasted sesame oil, ginger, yuzu kosho
faq: What is burdock root?

A popular vegetable in Japanese and Korean cuisine, known in Japanese as gobo. It is crispy and sweet, somewhat like jicama but a little more earthy, maybe like water chestnut. Find it at Asian grocers and well-stocked natural foods stores.
How do you make burdock chips in the microwave?

Shave thin pieces on a mandoline, lay them in a single layer on a plate and microwave on high 30 seconds at a time until shriveled and crispy but not burned, reducing the power for the last couple of cycles. Cool a minute, then pull up the crisps. If they stick, grease the plate with a drop of oil or pan spray.
Why does the microwave work as a dehydrator?
Microwaves excite the water molecules in food, so with thin slices you can evaporate the water right out. The same move works on vegetables from carrot to horseradish.
Do I need a ring mold?
No. If you don't have a 3 1/2 inch ring mold or biscuit cutter, layer the ingredients in a bowl; it will be just as good.
What else can I use the miso dressing on?
It is delicious on cucumbers or as a general-purpose salad dressing. If you don't have yuzu kosho, use a sriracha-style paste plus zest from 1 lime.

a couple of weeks at room temperature in an airtight container

summary: Aji amarillo hot sauce: toast 4 dried aji amarillo peppers about 20 seconds per side, remove stems, seeds and ribs, soak in boiling water 10 minutes or more, then puree with lemon juice, garlic and salt; yields about 1/4 cup.
glance: about 20 seconds on each side in a dry skillet
10 minutes or more in 1/4 cup boiling water
faq: What is aji amarillo?

One of the most important ingredients in Peruvian cuisine. The fresh pepper is used to make huancaina, a cheese sauce served on dishes like papa a la huancaina, cold potatoes with eggs. Dried, it tastes more like sundried tomato than the raisins of many peppers, and the heat level is quite high.
How do you make a hot sauce from dried chiles?

Briefly toast the peppers on a dry, hot skillet or griddle, remove the seeds, stems and ribs, soak the flesh in a bit of boiling water, then add salt and an acid such as citrus juice or vinegar plus any garlic, herbs or spices, and puree.
Why shouldn't I burn the peppers?
If you burn them they become bitter. Toast about 20 seconds per side, just until fragrant.
Can I use other dried chiles?
Yes, the recipe can be made with other dried chiles. Use more if they are small; these aji amarillos were about 5 inches long and 1 inch wide.
How do I handle hot chiles safely?
Wear disposable gloves. If you get a hot spot on your hands, rubbing alcohol is pretty effective at removing the oils.
How do I use the sauce?
Anywhere you would use a bottled hot sauce like Tabasco or Tapatio: a dab enlivens a taco or a plate of scrambled eggs.

summary: Zucchini and chickpea tagine, made in a skillet or Dutch oven with tagine-style flavors: sauteed zucchini, microwaved carrots and chickpeas simmered 10 minutes with cumin, cinnamon, dried mint, ras el hanout, Aleppo pepper, tomato paste and preserved lemon.
faq: Why is this called a tagine if it isn't made in one?
A tagine is the Moroccan clay pot with a conical lid used for slow-braised stews. Nothing here needs a long braise, so a skillet or Dutch oven works, but the flavorings are very typical of the genre.
What can I substitute for ras el hanout, Aleppo pepper or preserved lemon?
You can substitute or omit them. If you omit the ras el hanout, add more of the other spices; cayenne or chili flakes can stand in for Aleppo pepper.
Can I use canned chickpeas?
Yes: two 15-ounce cans, drained and rinsed, ones that are tender and not snappy. Home-cooked are preferred.
What do you serve with it?
Fluffy couscous and thick Greek yogurt, unless you are gluten free or vegan respectively.
Can I change the vegetables?
Yes. You can adapt the basic method with different vegetables and/or beans for a wide variety of easy, homey but very flavorful stews.

summary: Vegan "bacon" from king oyster mushrooms: slice lengthwise about 2mm thick on a mandoline, rub with salt, sugar, smoked paprika and pepper for at least 15 minutes, wipe, and pan-fry about 1 minute per side until golden.
glance: depends on the size and quantity of mushrooms
1 tablespoon Maldon, 2 tablespoons sugar, 2 tablespoons smoked paprika, 1/4 teaspoon pepper
about 1 minute per side, then 20 seconds or so to crisp as it cools
faq: How do you make mushroom bacon?

Slice king oyster mushrooms lengthwise to about 2mm, rub both sides with a dry rub of salt, sugar, smoked paprika and pepper, let sit at least 15 minutes, wipe off the excess and pan-fry in a thin layer of oil until golden, about 1 minute a side.
What do I slice the mushrooms with?
A mandoline is highly recommended; unless you have Morimoto-level knife skills, it is hard to cut them to a consistent thickness by hand.
How do I keep mushroom bacon crispy?
It crisps up as it cools, in about 20 seconds, on paper towels. It loses crispness when exposed to moisture for long, so add it at the last possible moment before serving.
What if it tastes bitter?
Halve the smoked paprika and increase the sugar.
How can I change the rub?
Add brown sugar, chilis, coriander, coffee, cumin, garlic or tomato powder.
What can I use it in?
Anything you would use bacon for: sandwiches, pasta, fried polenta.

summary: Vietnamese tofu sandwiches (banh mi chay): pan-fried tofu slabs with quick-pickled carrot and daikon, cucumber, onion, jalapeno, avocado, mint and cilantro, in crusty baguette rolls dressed with sriracha mayo.
glance: carrot and daikon in water, white vinegar and sugar
about 10 inches long, very crusty outside and fairly soft inside
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the mayo
faq: What is banh mi chay?
A Vietnamese sandwich made vegetarian: here pan-fried tofu with pickled carrot and daikon, cucumber, onion, jalapeno, avocado, mint and cilantro, with seasoned mayo.
What kind of bread for banh mi?

Baguette-style rolls about 10 inches long, seriously crusty on the outside and fairly soft in the crumb. Vietnamese ones are believed to include rice flour; otherwise use the best French baguette you can find.
How do I make it vegetarian at a restaurant?
The author notes that at Seattle Deli you have to ask them not to use fish sauce.
How could I add more flavor?
Flavor the mayo intensely with a chili sauce and/or citrus, marinate the tofu, or add drops of chili-flavored sesame oil.
How do I make the quick pickle?
Marinate the carrot and daikon batons in 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup white vinegar and 1/4 cup sugar.
Is banh mi chay vegan?
It is vegan if you omit the mayo.
